_note: AI constants. Every nation but the player's uses the same rules and the same default temperament; a scenario may override traits per nation (ai_traits) and give nations plans (ai_plans). Weights here are tuned in phase 6, step 8.

temperament._note: aggression and caution, 0 to 1. They scale the odds an AI wants before it attacks, the share of its army it commits and how readily it digs in or pulls back.

odds._note: Attacker power over defender power wanted before an advance: the bold (aggression 1, caution 0) ask for `bold`, the cautious (aggression 0, caution 1) for `cautious`.

value._note: AI.value of a province: its share of the owner's people and of its output (GDP plus industry), with a bonus when it is the capital.

threat._note: AI.threat: enemy power inside the province counts in full, power `hops` away is cut by `hop_decay` per hop; the sum is multiplied by 1 + stakes * value(province).

defense._note: reserve_share: share of a nation's power kept back as a reserve (scaled up by caution); needs reserve_min_armies armies. reserve_stay: the reserve moves only when another province is this many times more threatened than where it stands. merge_max_units: the most units in a stack the AI will form by merging. rebalance_ratio: an army changes front when one front is this many times better covered than another. retake_hops and retake_eta_spread: armies within that many hops, arriving within that many days of each other, may retake home ground.

offense._note: max_share: share of a nation's power an aggression of 1 puts on offence. Target utility = w_plan * plan weight + w_value * AI.value + w_score * war score share + w_margin * (power over required odds, up to 2) - w_days * days to arrive - w_supply * supply hops; a target below min_utility is not attacked. retry_days: wait after finding nothing to attack. gather_days: give up if the force is not ready by then. fall_back_morale (scaled by 0.5 + caution) and fall_back_ratio (own power over the enemy's around the target): below them the stack falls back. plan_hops: how far an objective's weight reaches. reach_hops: armies this near may be sent, and reinforce_weight: the share of the power of enemy armies within support_hops that counts against an attack.

forces._note: Recruiting. war_multiplier: war strength as a multiple of the peacetime army. per_turn: units started per turn. max_training: units in training at once. treasury_floor: the treasury is never taken below it, plus deficit_months of any deficit. income_share: units in training cost at most this share of horizon_months of revenue. train_hops: how far behind the most threatened line it raises. mix: share of each unit type in the force.

navy._note: AINavy and AILanding. Fleets of a nation at war are split by role in port (transports and submarines apart, and cruisers and destroyers detached as patrols) and then given a sea zone each: the cordon that would seal an enemy's ports from the open sea (a path-blocking search, narrowest zones first), the zones next to its own ports where enemy ships lie, and the zones where an escort is wanted for a landing. A zone's score = w_blockade / cordon size (or w_defend * its share of the nation's port trade, w_kill for a zone with enemy ships, w_escort) - w_days * days to get there; a fleet goes only where its power (with what is already sent there) is at least the nation's required odds times the enemy power in or around the zone (adjacent zones count adj_decay, fleets in port opening on it port_share). Below min_score it stays in, or goes to, port. A fleet whose nation is weaker (times sortie_ratio) than its enemies within theatre_hops zones of it seeks out neither the cordon nor the enemy's ships, only the waters by its ports; submarines go anyway. A zone already held by fleets sent there is worth stack_decay of its value to the next. repair_below / ready_strength: strength to go home and to sail again; range_factor: days at sea as a multiple of the shortest range before going home. replan_days: the pause between a fleet being given orders and a change of mind (it changes only for a gain of hysteresis). Landings: with no enemy ground across a land border, a nation with transports in port picks an enemy coast by AIOffense worth + w_margin * margin - w_days * days, needing power over the defenders times odds divided by the landing penalty; it gathers the armies (reach_hops by land) and the transports in the port, waits for its ships to hold the landing zone and the route (escort_days), then sends them. Building: at war, below build_ratio times the enemy fleets' power, one squadron at a time (max_building), by the type furthest below its share in the mix, if the treasury keeps build_floor, the cost in hand is within income_share of horizon_months of revenue and the budget carries the upkeep (tolerance of net).

budget._note: AIBudget, once a month. Taxes: up by tax_step (to tax_max, or tax_max_war at war) when the nation is in debt and cannot repay it in repay_months, or runs a deficit its treasury cannot carry for cushion_months; down toward the default when it is in surplus with more than rich_months of expenses in the bank. Programs: all dropped, one a month, when the treasury is under program_floor and the budget in deficit; the programs in program_order taken up, one a month, when the budget keeps program_margin after their cost and the treasury is twice program_floor. Buildings: one a month, at most max_construction at a time, only when net is at least build_min_net; among the candidates richest provinces, the capital and ground behind the fronts, the one with the best yearly return per pound (min_return; food counts food_value, a foreign ministry diplomacy_value while points are short, a railway near a front front_railway_bonus of the province's output, the capital times capital_multiplier), leaving build_floor in the treasury (double at war). Points: in a crisis, a batch is bought when the stock is under buy_below and buy_floor stays in the treasury.

production._note: AIProduction, once a month, after the budget. Lines: the military factories are shared by the automatic split bent toward the equipment the army lacks most by deficit_weight (nothing changes while nothing is lacking). Law: total_mobilization at war when the worst deficit is at least total_deficit and war support at least total_min_support; war_economy at war from war_deficit; early_mobilization at any war or from the mobilization level early_mobilization; otherwise civilian. Funding: at war a nation funds its army and navy at war_funding (as far as its law allows) while its treasury holds funding_months of expenses, else at the usual. Factories: AIBudget counts a military factory as worth factory_value times the worst deficit a year (times war_factor at war).

diplomacy._note: AIDiplomacy. join: value = kind[kind] + w_ally_relation * opinion of the ally + w_enemy_relation * dislike of the enemies + w_border * share of enemies at its border + w_odds * (own side's share of power - 0.5) * 2 + w_support * war support above 50 - w_debt * debt (in months of revenue, at most 1) + w_decline * what declining costs; it joins at threshold. war: desire = w_hostile * dislike + w_grievance * grievance + w_plan if it has a plan against the target + w_cb if it has a casus belli; it never declares on a nation it made peace with in the last truce_days, nor without a motive of at least min_motive (desire without the casus belli); it declares when desire * (0.5 + aggression) reaches declare_threshold and the odds (its side's power over the target's side, with allies and guarantors) reach its required odds times odds_margin. With no casus belli it also needs a plan, aggression of at least unjustified_min_aggression, odds of unjustified_odds, and room under the cap (unjustified_share_max in this file). treaties: once a month it may propose the treaty of greatest value at least propose_threshold (alliance: w_need * how much stronger a hostile neighbour is + w_bloc + w_relation; guarantee: w_menace * the menace to the guaranteed + w_bloc + w_relation; nap: w_need + w_relation; passage: w_passage when an enemy lies beyond a neutral) and improve relations with a friend (within improve_window of the alliance bar) or a strong neighbour (improve_threshold), always keeping points_reserve diplomacy points. rival_relation: a neighbour below it is a rival.

peace._note: AIPeace. urge = -score * k_score + k_support * (support_ref - war support, if positive) + k_debt * months of revenue owed (at most debt_cap_months) + k_days_per_month * months at war + capital_lost if the enemy holds the capital - k_ally * allies still fighting (less by ally_boldness_discount for the bold). A nation made to give accepts terms costing no more than its urge, if its score is at most -loss_floor or its urge is at least seek_threshold; a white peace is taken while urge is at least -white_tolerance; offered terms are taken if they cost at least accept_share of the taker's score. Past seek_threshold a nation proposes peace; with score at least demand_score and war aims met by aims_enough it names its price: up to demand_budget_share of its score in provinces (aims first), then an indemnity of at most indemnity_max_share over indemnity_months. afford_share: the most of its monthly revenue a nation will commit to indemnities.
